title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9613: loops unrolled (pass 1 by 8, pass 2 by 4, arrivals by 2), 593-instruction step

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9613 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It is this solver's 67772ed0 (125.9709: R = 2^20, checkpoint-only cycle detection, global anchor rounds, even-y key, rare-event and fused field kernels, the canonical-index rule with one-sided error bounds, and arrival rows executed as kernels/arrive.s) with only its loop control changed. Pass 1 runs eight walks per iteration with a group counter (826 instructions per 8 walks, 103.25 per walk); pass 2 runs four per iteration and ends when its slot pointer reaches slot 0, the slot array's only address with bit 22 clear (1,825 per 4 walks, 456.25 per walk); the arrival loop runs pairs of walks ending on the pointer array's end bit (32.5 per arrival). The 2^20 walks are split once into 24 batches of n = 1 (mod 8) walks (43,689 to 43,729), so the tails of (n - 1) mod 8 and (n - 1) mod 4 walks run only in rounds where walks double, at most 17.5 instructions per doubling, carried by the doubling price. Each walk body is emitted once as an assembler macro; experiment.py's interpreter expands the macros, executes the loops on production points against affine arithmetic (batches of 3, 6, 9, 17 and 25, exactly 103.25 and 456.25 per walk) and the arrival rows against the bit-exact model and the exact rule (32.5 per walk). The ordinary step is 593 = 103.25 + 456.25 + 33.5; doubling 761, traversal 626. The walk, H1 (kappa = 1.01, p0 = 0.3901753, h = 0.000165), the census, the store and the failure rows (sum 1.0103e-7 < 2e-7) are unchanged. Recovery probability is greater than 0.3900101 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^125.960122, hard extras = 2^114.564105, expected random extras = 2^102.1523, allowance = ceil(extras/0.000165) = 2^114.7175, W_ledger = 2^125.9612524 < 2^125.9613; Markov ratio 0.000152776 < 0.000165. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259613 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259612. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. Dependencies: 67772ed0, 2d25756c, 13c3295f, b5de673a, 6d5e2adb, 736c001a, f99114e0, 5d3bf6c4, 67154fda, daa13d54 and 02feb284. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk with the even-y key and per-trail anchor phases on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the generated field kernels (asserting every no-overflow step and the rare-event predicates, including the fused reductions) checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, the shipped counted loops (unrolled, with tail loops), emitter wrappers and arrival rows (kernels/arrive.s, by pairs, against a bit-exact model of the canonical-index rule and the exact rule) executed by an AArch64 interpreter that expands assembler macros (kernels/a64.py) (including constructed reduction inputs whose last addition carries, which must return the predicted z mod p - C0), instruction counts parsed from the shipped assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
